correctness.rationale: For every d>=2, MIO implies each equatorial qubit Pauli observable has a Hermitian traceless-contraction Heisenberg preimage. The polytope extreme-point proof establishes Tr H^2<=2 floor(d/2), including parity and equality vertices. HS duality gives the global upper bound without postselection. Explicit pair-combining SIO Kraus matrices are CPTP, preserve diagonals, and saturate on rho=I/d+epsilon Z for every 0<epsilon<1/d. Its input eigenvalues are strictly positive and the coherence norm ratio is exactly sqrt(floor(d/2)). Reconstructed formulas and successfully executed standalone verifier corroborate the algebra in dimensions 2..12; finite checks are not used as the all-d proof.

originality.rationale: The published 2015 counterexample establishes failure of Hilbert–Schmidt coherence monotonicity and, by discarding mixed ancillas, already provides the even-dimensional construction. The new claim is not that example: it proves the exact optimal amplification ratio for every MIO channel with qubit output, establishes dimension-parity dependence including the dimension-three boundary, and gives full-rank SIO optimizers. This statement was compared against relevant complete primary sources and targeted equivalent-formulation searches. An inaccessible 2020 coherence article remains a nontrivial priority risk, but its available abstract/first page does not supply a covering theorem.

value.rationale: The Hilbert–Schmidt off-diagonal norm is a natural but known-nonmonotone coherence statistic. An exact worst-case amplification invariant over all d-to-qubit MIO has an independent operational role in quantifying how badly it fails to be monotone. The dimension-three no-amplification boundary, unbounded sqrt(d) growth, and full-rank SIO attainment distinguish the complete classification from known easy counterexamples or a normalization exercise. It claims no higher-output result or quantum advantage from the invalid monotone.
